html:
A steel arch bridge across Sydney Harbour, opened in 1932, that joins the city centre to the North Shore. With the Opera House beside it, it is the classic image of Sydney.

Engineers had dreamed of a crossing since the 1800s. The project was led by John Bradfield of the New South Wales public works department, and the British firm Dorman Long of Middlesbrough won the contract. Work began in 1923. The two halves of the arch were built out from each shore, held back by cables, until they met in 1930. Locals nicknamed it "the Coathanger".

It opened in March 1932, in the depths of the Great Depression, and gave work to many men when jobs were scarce. At the opening a man from a right-wing group rode up on a horse and cut the ribbon with his sword before the premier could.

The bridge carries cars, trains, bikes and walkers. It is still one of the widest long-span bridges in the world, and its arch is the centre of Sydney's New Year fireworks.
sum: A steel arch bridge across Sydney Harbour, opened in 1932, that joins the city centre to the North Shore. With the Opera House beside it, it is the classic image of Sydney.
